description: This line plot illustrates the number of shared experts for two samples across different task domains as a function of sample token count, using a logarithmic x-axis ranging from $2^9$ to $2^{20}$ tokens and a linear y-axis ranging from 2.0 to 6.0 shared experts. The plot compares six domains: Intent (orange solid line), Summary (blue solid line), Law (yellow solid line), Translation (purple solid line), Code (gray solid line), and Math (green solid line). The “Intent” line starts near 3.8 at $2^9$, dips to ~3.9 at $2^{11}$, then rises steadily to ~5.95 at $2^{20}$. The “Summary” line begins at ~1.95, climbs sharply to ~5.8 by $2^{15}$, and plateaus near 5.95. The “Law” line starts at ~3.6, fluctuates between 4.5 and 5.7, and stabilizes near 5.95. The “Translation” line begins at ~5.1, dips to ~4.7 at $2^{11}$, rises to ~5.6 at $2^{13}$, and converges near 5.95. The “Code” line starts at ~1.95, rises gradually with minor dips (e.g., to ~3.1 at $2^{13}$ and ~3.05 at $2^{14}$), and reaches ~5.75 at $2^{20}$. The “Math” line begins at ~3.8, increases steadily to ~5.95 by $2^{18}$, and remains flat thereafter. All lines except “Code” converge near the upper limit of the y-axis at higher token counts, indicating saturation in shared expert usage.
